papers.symbols:
$h,w,y,n,\delta(n)$
Annual market hours (thousands), hourly wage in dollars, annual net expenditure in thousands of dollars, number of children, and $\delta(n)=\sqrt n$ with $\delta(0)=0$ and $\delta(1)=1$.
$t,k,c,m,T_c,f,\lambda,u_f,u_c$
Childcare hours, purchased care, own and children’s consumption, required care, childcare technology, altruism weight, and mother’s/child’s preferences.
$e_t,e_m,e,a_t,a_m,a,b_t,b_m$
Time, monetary and composite child costs; fixed cost components with $a=a_t+a_m$; childcare time per child (thousands of hours); dimensionless marginal share of nonlabor income spent on children.
$F,F'_1,F'_2$
Childless labor-supply function and wage/resource derivatives; preference stability keeps this reference behavior across parental status.
$\alpha_0,\ldots,\alpha_5,z^h$
Baseline coefficients; hours controls contain a constant, age, age squared, Black and Hispanic indicators. Starred coefficients are the translated linear specification.
$z^w,z^y, eta_w, eta_y,\sigma_ u,\sigma_\mu, u,\mu$
Wage/resource controls and coefficients, error scales, and standardized errors. Wage controls add education; resource instruments add asset, welfare, transfer and other incomes and their squares.
$u, ho_\mu, ho_ u,\sigma_\epsilon,\epsilon,\widehat\mu,h_0,w_0$
Hours disturbance and control-function coefficients; standardized hours error; estimated resource residual; deterministic hours/wage components. $ u$ and $\epsilon$ are normally distributed; the hat indicates an estimate.

$q$ denotes remaining resources after child costs in the quadratic specification.

**Quadratic specification translated by children, with control functions and participation (equations 16–18, 22–25).** The linear baseline (19) above is the nested special case.

$$
\begin{aligned}
q&=y-a\delta(n)-b_t\delta(n)w-b_m\delta(n)y,\\
h_0(w)&=\alpha_0 z^h+\alpha_1w+\alpha_2q+\alpha_3w^2+\alpha_4q^2+\alpha_5qw-b_t\delta(n),\\
w_0&=\beta_w z^w,\qquad w=w_0+\sigma_\nu\nu,\\
y&=\beta_y z^y+\sigma_\mu\mu,\\
u&=\rho_\mu\widehat\mu+\rho_\nu\nu+\sigma_\epsilon\epsilon,\\
h&=\begin{cases}
h_0(w)+\rho_\mu\widehat\mu+\rho_\nu(w-w_0)/\sigma_\nu+\sigma_\epsilon\epsilon,&\text{if this expression is positive},\\
0,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\end{aligned}
$$

Here $q$ is shorthand for the translated resource argument, not a separately observed quantity. Working women contribute the hours density; non-participants contribute the probability of zero hours integrated over their latent wage.
